structuralDecisions.decision: internal/docstyle is a new, flat utility package — Finding, markdown classification, and each rule (sentences, vocabulary, modals, passive, dictionary, ignore) live as sibling files in one package, with Check(paths []string) (Report, error) as the single public entrypoint. No Entities/UseCases/Adapters sub-packages.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Verified against existing sibling packages (internal/patternspec, internal/testlint, internal/diffcover): each is a flat, single-purpose package with one exported entrypoint consumed directly by a cmd/loom/cmd/*.go file — none splits into Clean Architecture sub-layers. go-conventions.md's Entities→UseCases→Adapters→Frameworks layering governs services with real domain/use-case/adapter separation and multiple consumers; a stateless, file-in/report-out lint utility with one consumer does not have that shape, and pre-splitting it would be the Premature Generalization anti-pattern named in design-principles.md. Reversibility: Cheap — splitting later, if a second consumer appears, is a mechanical extraction.
tradeOffs: If docstyle later gains a second consumer with different formatting needs, Render/Report may need an interface extracted from report.go at that point — deliberately deferred, not pre-built.

fitness.property: internal/docstyle is imported only by cmd/loom/cmd/docs_check.go and its own tests; no reverse dependency from internal/docstyle back into cmd/loom/cmd exists
fitness.verification: go build ./... — Go's own import-cycle rules and the existing cmd→internal dependency direction make the reverse import impossible without an explicit, visible new import; no new lint rule needed beyond the existing build

structuralDecisions.decision: Add a `strict bool` field to the existing shared docsFlags struct in cmd/loom/cmd/docs.go (not a separate flags struct for docs_check.go), and register docsCheckCmd in the same init() alongside docsPlanCmd/docsApproveCmd/docsApplyCmd.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Confirmed in cmd/loom/cmd/docs_test.go: runDocsCommand's helper does `docsArgs = flags` wholesale and every existing docs subcommand test reuses that one package-level docsFlags struct, even for fields scoped to a single subcommand (inTreeReadmes, docComments, noCodemap, codemapOnly are all plan-only, yet live in the shared struct, not a plan-specific one). Matching that precedent lets docs_check_test.go reuse the exact same test harness rather than introducing a second, inconsistent flags convention for one new subcommand. Reversibility: Cheap.
tradeOffs: docsFlags keeps accumulating fields that only one subcommand reads — accepted existing debt (see refactoring opportunity below), not newly introduced by this feature, and not this feature's job to fix.

fitness.property: docs_check_test.go compiles against and calls the existing runDocsCommand(t, run, flags, input, args...) helper, exactly like the plan/approve/apply tests

structuralDecisions.decision: Finding is a new type in internal/docstyle/finding.go — Finding{File, Line, Rule, Excerpt} with String() rendering `file:line: rule: excerpt`. It does not reuse or extend internal/patternspec.Issue.
structuralDecisions.rationale: patternspec.Issue.String() renders 'file: field: message' (no Line field, a Severity field this feature has no use for) for a different bounded context — Pattern Spec validation, per DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md — not doc style checking. Bending Issue to a second shape and a second meaning would be a Leaky Abstraction; a new four-field value type is cheaper and clearer. Reversibility: Cheap.

fitness.verification: internal/docstyle/finding_test.go asserts the exact rendered string for a representative Finding

structuralDecisions.decision: internal/docstyle/dictionary.go reimplements the table-row/backtick/comma-split parsing approach already proven in shared/mcp/internal/analyzers/ubiquitous_language_analyzer.go (tableRowRe-equivalent regex, synonym comma/backtick splitting, parenthetical-note trimming) rather than importing that package.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Confirmed via go.mod: this repo's module root is github.com/orieken/loom; shared/mcp/internal/analyzers sits under a different internal/ visibility root (shared/mcp/), so Go's compiler refuses the import outright from internal/docstyle. There is no refactor that preserves both packages' internal/ privacy and shares the code without first exporting it from a non-internal location, which is out of this feature's scope. Verified DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md's live table format (`| **Term** | Domain | Description | Synonyms to AVOID |`, backtick-quoted comma lists, trailing parenthetical notes like '(too generic)') matches what the existing analyzer already parses, so copying its proven regex shape is lower-risk than inventing a new one.
tradeOffs: A future change to DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md's table format must be hand-applied to both parsers; nothing mechanically keeps them in sync.

structuralDecisions.decision: The noun-cluster rule (writing-style.md's '>3 consecutive nouns') is explicitly not implemented, and that omission is itself a checked, testable fact — stated in `loom docs check`'s own help/Long text and in shared/rules/writing-style.md, in closely matching wording.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Per AC3's escape hatch: reliable consecutive-noun detection needs part-of-speech tagging unavailable in go.mod or the Go standard library; a crude capitalization/word-list heuristic would not deterministically check the grammatical property the rule names and would generate findings a human then has to triage, which is worse than silence. Recording the decision turns an invisible gap into a visible, verified one rather than an implied-but-false claim of full coverage. Reversibility: Cheap — reverses the moment a POS tagger is deliberately adopted, which would be its own decision given the 'no new dependency' constraint.

fitness.property: `loom docs check --help` and shared/rules/writing-style.md both state that the noun-cluster rule is not mechanically checked by this command
fitness.verification: cmd/loom/cmd/docs_check_test.go asserts the command's help/Long text contains the noun-cluster exclusion note; a second test greps shared/rules/writing-style.md for the matching note

structuralDecisions.decision: Check() returns Findings sorted by file then line; docs_check.go signals a --strict failure with a package-level sentinel error (e.g. errDocStyleFindingsFound) and relies entirely on cmd/loom/cmd/root.go's existing cobra.CheckErr(err) fallthrough for the exit(1) — root.go itself is not touched.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Confirmed in root.go's Execute(): a short list of named sentinel errors (errHealthFailed, errStateVerifyFailed, orchestrator.ErrWaitingApproval, orchestrator.ErrBudgetExhausted, context.Canceled) get special exit codes, then any other non-nil error falls through to cobra.CheckErr(err), which exits 1. AC1 only needs plain 0/1, no special code, so a plain sentinel reaching that fallthrough is correct and needs zero root.go changes. Reversibility: Cheap.

fitness.property: `loom docs check --strict` exits 1 when Findings is non-empty and 0 otherwise; default mode always exits 0
fitness.verification: cmd/loom/cmd/docs_check_test.go — three cases: default exit 0 with findings present, --strict exit 1 with findings present, --strict exit 0 with zero findings

structuralDecisions.decision: No stability patterns (CircuitBreaker, retries, timeouts) are introduced for internal/docstyle.
structuralDecisions.rationale: architecture-guardrails.md #5 governs network calls; this feature's own NFR states it makes none — it reads only the file paths given on the command line and DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md from local disk. Adding resilience machinery here would be unjustified ceremony for synchronous local file reads.

fitness.property: internal/docstyle imports no net/http, database/sql, or queue client package
fitness.verification: go list -deps ./internal/docstyle/... reviewed in code review; no CI gate is proposed since nothing here currently imports any network package

componentPlacement.reason: Value type carrying File, Line, Rule, Excerpt; no behavior beyond String().

AC3's 20/25-word thresholds, list-step vs descriptive-sentence tagging.
AC's per-file 'to be' + past-participle share heuristic, labelled as an estimate.
AC5's Synonyms-to-AVOID table parsing and skip-list; see structural decision on duplication across the Go internal/ visibility boundary.
Recognizes the ignore comment, suppresses the next finding, counts suppressions.
Single public entrypoint: walks paths, strips ignored regions, runs every rule, applies suppression, aggregates and sorts the Report. The one place that knows the full rule list.
Converts the in-memory Report into the `file:line: rule: excerpt` text format plus the skipped-count summary line — the output-formatting boundary.
The outermost cobra.Command layer: parses --strict, calls docstyle.Check, prints via cmd.OutOrStdout(), returns the sentinel error on --strict failure.
Extends the existing shared flags struct and init() wiring — see structural decision 2.

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: internal/docstyle (Use Case/Domain) must not import cmd/loom/cmd/* (Framework layer)
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: Confirmed no internal/* package in this repo imports cmd/loom/cmd; the dependency direction is always cmd → internal, matching Clean Architecture's inward-pointing rule. No docstyle code needs anything cmd-layer provides.

Go's internal/ visibility refuses this import outright — confirmed the two packages sit under different module-relative internal/ roots (shared/mcp/ vs the repo module root). This is why dictionary.go reimplements rather than imports (structural decision above).

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: cmd/loom/cmd/docs_check.go (Framework/CLI) may import internal/docstyle (Use Case) — correct inward-to-outward direction
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: Outer layer depending on inner layer is the Clean Architecture direction; no violation.

antiPatternChecks.pattern: Duplication (pattern, not bug) across an internal/ visibility boundary
antiPatternChecks.notes: dictionary.go knowingly duplicates ubiquitous_language_analyzer.go's table-parsing regex approach because Go's internal/ visibility makes importing it impossible. Accepted and documented, not a defect — see the dedicated structural decision.

Considered and rejected a Strategy-pattern per-rule plugin interface. design-principles.md reserves Strategy for behavior that varies by context; here the rule set is fixed and small (5 mechanized rules), so a dispatch-map/interface is speculative. Plain functions called in sequence from check.go is the simplest design that satisfies AC7.
Adding a 6th rule later touches exactly two places — a new <rule>.go file and one call from check.go — not shotgun surgery.
check.go orchestrates but each rule's logic lives in its own file; no single file does sentence-splitting, vocabulary matching, modal detection, passive detection, and dictionary parsing.
Not applicable in the DDD sense — this is a stateless report generator, not a persisted-entity system; Finding is a plain value type by design, not an entity missing behavior.

refactoringOpportunities.reason: docsFlags will carry 8 fields spanning 4 unrelated subcommands' flags after this feature (root is persistent; run/inTreeReadmes/docComments/noCodemap/codemapOnly/yes are plan/approve-specific; strict is check-specific) — a Data Clump per subcommand. Not pursued now: it would touch the existing plan/approve/apply tests for no behavior change, which is out of this feature's scope. Flagged for a future pass if a 5th or 6th subcommand makes the shared struct noisier.

developerHandoffNotes: internal/docstyle stays flat — one package, Check(paths []string) (Report, error) is the only symbol cmd/loom/cmd/docs_check.go calls. No sub-packages.
Add `strict bool` to docsFlags in cmd/loom/cmd/docs.go and register docsCheckCmd via docsCmd.AddCommand(docsPlanCmd, docsApproveCmd, docsApplyCmd, docsCheckCmd) in the existing init().

Print all report output through cmd.OutOrStdout() (matches docs.go:101,135,215), never fmt.Println/os.Stdout directly, so docs_check_test.go can capture it the same way docs_test.go's runDocsCommand helper does.

Define one package-level sentinel error (e.g. errDocStyleFindingsFound) in docs_check.go. Return nil unless --strict && len(report.Findings) > 0. Do not touch root.go — its existing cobra.CheckErr(err) fallthrough already turns any other non-nil error into exit 1.

dictionary.go must not try to import shared/mcp/internal/analyzers — Go will refuse it. Copy the regex approach (table-row match, backtick/comma synonym split, parenthetical-note trimming), don't attempt to share code across that internal/ boundary.
Put the noun-cluster omission note in both docsCheckCmd's help/Long text and shared/rules/writing-style.md in closely matching wording — a test checks both.
Sort Report.Findings by file then line in Check() so output is deterministic across test runs and across OS directory-walk orderings.
